items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
A bee sting and a toothache open the lesson.

Litmus shows only acid or base, so we bring in the **pH scale** and **universal indicator**, and classify solutions from pH-paper results.

pH then explains **antacids, tooth decay, soil treatment and stings**; we end by separating **strong and weak** acids from **concentrated and dilute** ones.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• litmus, phenolphthalein and methyl orange as indicators

• $\mathrm{H^{+}}$(aq) and $\mathrm{OH^{-}}$(aq) ions in acids and bases; neutralisation

• dilution lowers the concentration of ions

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** Interpret the pH scale.

**2.** Use universal indicator results to classify solutions.

**3.** Explain pH in digestion, antacids and tooth decay.

**4.** Explain pH in soil and in bee and nettle stings.

**5.** Tell strong and weak from concentrated and dilute.

chunks.name: A bee sting and a toothache

items.text:
**What this shows**

• Left: a bee has stung a boy at a picnic. His grandmother puts baking soda paste on the sting; a lemon lies beside it.

• Right: the boy at the dentist with a hole in his tooth. Toffees and toothpaste are on the tray.

**Answer to Question 1**

The sting leaves an **acid**; baking soda is a **base**, so it cancels the acid. Lemon juice is an acid itself.

items.text:
**Answer to Question 3**

**No.** Litmus tells only whether a solution is an acid or a base, not **how acidic** it is.

**What this shows**

The pH scale from 0 to 14, with 7 marked neutral.

**Answer to Question 4**

**(a)** A has more $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ions.

**(b)** A is acidic, B is basic: the higher the $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ion concentration, the lower the pH.

items.prompt: A liquid is added to a solution of pH 6, and the pH falls to 3. What has happened to the solution?
options: more acidic; its $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ion concentration has gone up
more acidic; its $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ion concentration has gone down
less acidic; its $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ion concentration has gone up
less acidic; its $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ion concentration has gone down

items.text:
**On this question**

**A**: a **lower pH** means **more** $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ions, so the solution is **more acidic**.

chunks.name: Too much acid in the stomach

items.text:
**Answer to Question 6**

A **mild base** neutralises the extra acid safely. Sodium hydroxide is **strongly basic and corrosive**: it would harm the mouth and stomach.

**What this shows**

How the pH in the mouth changes in the hour after eating a sweet. The dashed line marks pH 5.5; the shaded part is below it.

**Answer to Question 7**

**(a)** About **20 minutes** (from about 5 to 25 minutes, the shaded part).

**(b)** Each sweet starts a new dip, so the teeth spend much longer below pH 5.5.

script.x: Show the graph. Pointer 1 sets it up.

items.prompt: Tooth decay starts when the pH in the mouth falls below ______. Toothpaste, being ______, neutralises the excess acid.

items.text:
**On this question**

**A**: enamel is corroded below **pH 5.5**; toothpaste is **basic**, so it neutralises the acid.

items.text:
**What this shows**

Equal lengths of magnesium ribbon in dilute hydrochloric acid (A) and dilute acetic acid (B), the same amount at the same concentration.

**Answer to Question 10**

**(a)** A.

**(b)** Hydrochloric acid gives **more** $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ions than acetic acid of the same concentration, so hydrogen forms faster.

items.text:
**What this shows**

Acid particles in four beakers of water: a strong and a weak acid, each concentrated and dilute.

**Answer to Question 11**

**Concentrated or dilute**: how much acid is dissolved in a given volume of water.

**Strong or weak**: how much of the acid splits into $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ions.

script.x: Show the four beakers. Pointer 1 sets them up.

items.text:
**What this shows**

The same four beakers: a strong and a weak acid, each concentrated and dilute.

**Answer to Question 12**

**(a)** Beaker (a), with 6 $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ions.

**(b)** (b) and (c) have 2 each: a dilute strong acid can be as acidic as a concentrated weak acid.

**D**: dilution changes the **concentration**, not the **strength**.
